scope: Independent Studio source, regression and security review; actual browser acceptance is recorded separately by the root agent.
instructions: Read AGENTS.md and root assignment; neither AGENTS.md nor prior readiness/evidence/provenance files were modified.

leadA.existingBehavior: _get, _mutate, ingestion and authorizer errors already reuse sanitizeTelemetry(errorRecord(error, { stack: false })); invalid HTTP status falls back to 500 and oversized records keep a safe separately sanitized code.
leadA.coverage: Authorized actual-loopback read/mutation exceptions with bearer messages, secret-keyed, cyclic, BigInt and oversized details; ingestion and custom-authorizer exceptions; bounded JSON and no stack disclosure.
leadA.newFinding: Page rendering, asset reads, Prometheus generation and stream admission propagated errors to the host without the controller's bounded error response. Stream capacity/closed errors also bypassed the response boundary.
leadA.repair: Route those pre-header failures through the existing _failure method. Once headers have been sent, rethrow to the response's transport owner rather than attempt a second JSON response.
leadA.newCoverage: Synthetic controller errors across page/asset/Prometheus/stream, safe 503 stream capacity/closed responses and client listener cleanup, no second response after headers, plus actual-loopback Prometheus/stream redaction with cyclic and BigInt details.

leadB.coverage: Cancel each silence prompt independently and incident resolution: no mutation, no changed state. Deliberate empty rule ID preserves all-rules silence. Finite positive duration, intentional actions, visible failure, duplicate submission guard, delayed/non-cooperative action navigation and unmount, retained detail inspection/filter/focus, explicit resume, repeated mount/destroy and single stream ownership all pass focused fixtures.
leadB.modelLimit: Modeled DOM fixtures do not establish actual browser behavior; the root agent performs that separate gate.

additionalFinding.problem: MonitorStudioRateLimiter inserted rejected new-client buckets without applying maxKeys. With capacity 1 and mutation cost 5, distinct rejected clients exceeded the configured two-key cap.
additionalFinding.repair: Apply existing oldest-key eviction to the rejection path as well as the accepted path.
additionalFinding.coverage: Twenty rejected distinct clients remain at or below maxKeys 2; rejection counters and eviction counts are correct; accepted admission, subsequent denial and ordinary refill remain available.

commands.reason: All four loopback tests were denied listen EPERM 127.0.0.1 by the sandbox; this was an environment failure.

failures: Rejected clients obey the same key bound as accepted clients assertion
Uncaught synthetic route error with bearer message and details

commands.phase: final focused suite with approved loopback execution

compatibility: No export/declaration changes. Successful responses and operator actions are unchanged. Pre-header exceptional responses are now safe JSON instead of host-dependent uncaught failures. The configured client-key bound now applies equally to rejected and accepted traffic.
unchangedBoundaries: Existing socket/Host/origin/custom-authorizer checks, disabled remote ingestion default, memory-only token/polling policy, SSE ownership/queue limits, package release guards and existing dirty client/UI changes are preserved.
limitations: Custom capabilities and host transport handlers remain trusted application code. Pattern/key redaction is not universal secret detection. No browser assertion or production integration claim is made by this focused review; exact final archive verification is owned by the root agent.
